_comment: perception_spots.json - things a perceptive character notices (Scripts/perception_watcher.gd). Per zone, each spot has a place ([x, z]) and a radius in metres; walking within it rolls d20 + Wisdom modifier + Perception skill / 10 against each notice's 'dc' (D&D style: 10 easy, 15 medium, 20 hard). A success prints the notice in the chat once per character; a failure can be rolled again after 'retry_seconds'. Every roll trains Perception. Optional per notice: 'night': true (only at night) / false (only by day). ALL LINES ARE DRAFTS for the user to change; positions come from the zone's markers and spawn areas.

notices.text: Fresh scratches score the gate's iron bands, low down, as if something small tried very hard to claw its way in.
One stone in the gate arch is newer than the rest. Someone repaired a breach here and matched the colour almost perfectly.
Cut faintly into the underside of the arch, where no guard would look up: a closed eye over three drops. It has been scratched out, but not well enough.
The two spires lean very slightly toward each other, as if listening.
Sand has drifted against the east side of both spires, but not the west. The wind here only ever comes from the dunes.
For a heartbeat the tip of each spire burns with a thin violet flame. Then it is gone, and the stone is cold.
The planks are worn smooth in a path from the harbour master's post to the water's edge, where no boat is moored.
A rope tied to the last post trails down into the water. Whatever is on the other end is heavy, and nobody has pulled it up.
Among the gull tracks in the wet sand, a line of bare footprints walks up out of the sea and stops.
The mausoleum door has been forced. The hinges are bent outward: it was opened from the inside.
Fresh candle wax on the step, and a dried date left as an offering. Someone still visits.
Under the dust, the floor stones are laid in a spiral that leads nowhere. Or down.
Several graves have been dug up. Not robbed: the earth is heaped on the inside of the holes.
The newest headstones all carry the same flame of the Oasis Wardens. Too many of them for a quiet frontier.
One grave is freshly tended, its sand raked in neat lines, and the name on it is only half carved.

lumora_outskirts.name: The wreck on the south road

notices.text: The wagon wasn't ambushed on the road. The wheel ruts leave it well before the wreck: the driver was running.
The strongbox bolts were cut, not broken. Whoever took it came with the right tools.
A scrap of Djhanid sand-silk is caught on a splintered board. The Djhanid don't rob caravans. Someone wants it to look as if they do.
Someone has added a fourth arm to the signpost, pointing south, then sawn it off again.
Carved small at the foot of the post, in a traveller's hand: 'The water-debt is paid in shade.'
Most of the arrows in the targets are grouped tight and high. One archer here is very good, and practises alone.
A few old arrowheads in the far target are black glass, not iron. Djhanid work, and not recent.
The webs here are thicker than they should be, and faintly warm when the wind moves them.
Among the bones in the webs are a Warden's buckle and a scout's boot. The den has been feeding well.
The silk nearest the heart of the den has a faint purple sheen, like the edge of a Veilfire.
The goblins have dug a latrine, a cook pit and a lookout. This isn't a raiding camp. They mean to stay.
Stacked behind the tents: Lumoran grain sacks, still sealed. Whoever sold them to the goblins was paid well.
The chieftain's banner pole is capped with a bone carved into a closed eye.
Good boots by the fire, and fine cups. These brigands eat better than the guards at the gate.
A ledger lies half-burned in the fire pit. What survives lists caravans, days and times — the Sandveil Bazaar's own schedule.
